findings.description: The shipped F4 resume is O(offset) ordered rows per run and O(N^2/QueueCapacity) cumulative skip work per full cycle, where N is the server-wide movie+episode candidate count (the enumerator query is not library-scoped). This work executes on every scheduled (default 12h) and post-scan run.
findings.detail: The pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 host exposes no keyset/after-key predicate and no identifier-stable candidate order, so the identity-anchored locate must walk host-ordered pages from offset 0. ADR-029 clause 3 explicitly accepts this as the cost of the only host-supported mechanism and registers it; task 19.5 recorded it as accepted residual V12-F4-1 (MEDIUM) with a per-library (ParentId-scoped) enumerator + per-library cursors noted as the possible future mitigation. The code matches the accepted mechanism (JellyfinMediaLibraryEnumerator.ResumeCandidatesAsync walks bounded pages; JellyfinMediaLibraryEnumerator.CreateQuery sets only Recursive/IncludeItemTypes/OrderBy, i.e. server-wide). This is a material future risk for large libraries but it is user-approved, registered, and does not block Gate 19.
findings.recommended_action: None for Gate 19; the cost is honestly registered and accepted. Carry V12-F4-1 into the release review, and consider the registered per-library-enumerator mitigation as post-v1.2 backlog if load proves it necessary.

findings.description: Task 19.4's chain facts assert processor.PeakConcurrency(subjectKey) == 1 while every fact builds the worker with workerCount: 1, so that assertion cannot fail regardless of queue mechanics, and the 19.4 worker report cites it as 'chain-level single-flight' proof.
findings.detail: The authoritative single-flight evidence is the queue-level fact WorkItemKeyRemainsVersionBlindAndSingleFlightIsPerItemConnectionAndSurface, which exercises the real LibraryWorkQueue directly (version-only difference coalesces; a distinct surface is admitted while the primary key is in flight). The behavior is covered; the chain-fact assertion is redundant and the worker-report wording slightly overstates it. This is an open LOW already recorded by the 19.4 test-quality review (TQ-19.4-01) and does not affect any phase acceptance criterion.
findings.recommended_action: No change required for Gate 19. If hardened later, run two or more workers for the chain assertion or attribute single-flight solely to the queue-level fact.

findings.description: The no-extra-pass guard in both the 19.3 and 19.4 matrices is a fixed 250 ms wall-clock window (AssertStableAsync); a defect whose extra pass is delayed beyond 250 ms would escape it.
findings.detail: The window is bounded and asserts on every 10 ms sample (it cannot pass vacuously), and the defects the matrices detect are synchronous in-process enqueues, so the residual risk is low. This is the open LOW TQ-19.4-02. The matrices re-ran green repeatedly under the task reviewers and my independent focused runs.
findings.recommended_action: No change required for Gate 19. If the suite is hardened later, prefer a quiescence signal over a fixed wall-clock window.

summary: Phase 19 is complete and approved with findings. All five tasks in the authoritative execution order 19.1-19.5 passed the worker -> reviewer (with test-quality reviewers on 19.2/19.4) -> commit pipeline; each has a preserved attempt-1 report, a rework attempt where applicable (19.1 R-19.1-01 MEDIUM, 19.5 R-19.5-01 MEDIUM, both visibly closed in attempt-2 reports plus orchestration rework entries), and a commit whose contents match the reviewed change set (5093f2a, 2db423f, 65db3a5, 4ba029d, 478de28). I independently inspected the shipped implementation and it conforms to ADR-022 as amended by ADR-029 (persisted bounded Cache-authority (SortName, itemId) cursor; identity-anchored resume by unique itemId via bounded linear skip with no after-key host predicate; Accepted/Coalesced/InFlight covered, Overflow/Stopped stop with the cursor advanced only over the covered prefix; wrap; scheduled/post-scan only; scope and missing/torn reset) and to ADR-023 (bounded DiscardReason; exactly one current-version re-enqueue for ConfigurationStale after CompleteProcessing releases the in-flight slot; stopped/full bounded drop; version-blind WorkItemKey and single-flight unchanged). F4 and F6 are correctly removed from the open register and recorded resolved, each qualified by honestly registered, source-severity-matched residuals (V12-F4-1..6, V12-F6-1..2) consistent across open.md/archive.md/accepted.md/00-index.md/state.json; architecture section 8 and the Phase 19 changelog are accurate and non-overclaiming about the O(offset)/O(N^2) bound, the exact-(SortName, Name)-tie caveat, the unlocatable-anchor reset, the cache-TTL interaction, the overlapping-run effect, the host-order internal-detail risk, the artwork-stage window, and the unlogged bounded drop. I reproduced the validation independently: build 0 warnings / 0 errors; default suite Failed 0 / Passed 1901 / Skipped 64 / Total 1965; F4 focused 90/90; F6 focused 44/44; scripts/check-docs.sh PASS. Phase 19 in docs/plan/state.json remains status PLANNED with no gate_record and no v1.2.0-phase19 tag; the orchestrator applies the gate. No BLOCKER or HIGH finding is open; the remaining findings are one MEDIUM (the already-registered, user-accepted F4 skip cost over the server-wide candidate set) and LOW/INFORMATIONAL items (missing phase orchestration aggregate to be created at gate time, two open test-quality LOWs, the absent live-host run, the historical architecture-review status, and the accepted-plan snapshot).
